target.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveInitialCronDelivery` in `src/cron/service/initial-delivery.ts` only checks `sessionTarget === "isolated"` when deciding whether to inject default `{ mode: "announce" }` delivery. All other cron code paths already treat `"isolated"`, `"current"`, and `"session:"` as equivalent for this purpose, creating an inconsistency.

## Why This Change Was Made

After #98947 restored persistent session targets, the three sessionTarget values are treated identically in:
- `delivery-plan.ts:106-114` — `isDetachedOutputJob` check
- `normalize.ts:680-684` — `isDetachedDeliveryJob` check
- `jobs.ts:288-298` — `isIsolatedLike` check

But `initial-delivery.ts` was not updated, so cron jobs created with `--session-target current` or `--session-target session:...` would not get the default announce delivery at creation time.

## User Impact

Users creating cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "current"` or `"session:"` may miss delivery announcements.

## Evidence

**Exact head:** `afceffd830f0df94e315326ff8854e3ce99c19a8`

**End-to-end behavior proof (real gateway from the worktree at exact head, repo mock OpenAI, bundled `qa-channel` + in-repo QA bus; isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; no real credentials):** for BOTH `current` and `session:*` targets — CLI `cron add` creation → persisted delivery state (`cron list --json` + SQLite `cron_jobs`: `delivery_mode=announce`, `delivery_channel=last`) → `cron run` execution (the `session:*` job ran inside the persistent session `agent:main:qa-channel:channel:channel:qa-room`) → exactly one observed announcement per job delivered to the session channel (`qa-channel:channel:qa-room`). Full redacted transcripts: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99115#issuecomment-4985152103

**Regression coverage placement:** the direct-service contract is now documented in `src/cron/service/initial-delivery.ts` (supported creation paths fill delivery in `normalizeCronJobCreate`; this helper governs direct-service `CronService.add`/declarative-convergence callers and stays consistent with `src/cron/normalize.ts` + `src/cron/delivery-plan.ts`), with caller-level tests through the public `CronService.add` contract added in `src/cron/service/initial-delivery.test.ts`.

**Validation (exact head):**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/initial-delivery.test.ts --run`: 16/16 passed
- Neighboring cron suites (`normalize.test.ts`, `service.jobs.test.ts`, `service.declarative-jobs.test.ts`, `delivery-plan.test.ts`): 145/145 passed

Per-agent `agentDir` bootstrap files (`SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `TOOLS.md`, etc.) were silently ignored when `agentDir` differed from `workspaceDir`. Replaces blocking synchronous filesystem/Keychain I/O with async equivalents in auth/credential paths. Closes #78805

- Behavior or issue addressed: Gateway event loop blocking during credential reads
- Real environment tested: macOS with Claude Code and Codex CLI credentials in Keychain
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```
vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts \
    src/agents/cli-credentials.test.ts \
    src/agents/cli-auth-epoch.test.ts \
    src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.test.ts

vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts \
    src/gateway/resolve-configured-secret-input-string.test.ts
```
- Evidence after fix: 4 test files, 61 tests passed (vitest 4.1.8)
- Observed result after fix: All async credential paths return results without blocking the event loop
- What was not tested: Live Codex Keychain access on real macOS device (unit tests mock exec)
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Keychain access requires macOS; mocked in CI

## Tests and validation

- Commands: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts` and `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts`
- Regression coverage: Existing credential reader tests plus new async variant tests
- Before: `execSync("security find-generic-password")` blocked event loop for 4+ seconds
- After: `execAsync` returns immediately without blocking

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? No
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — credential reads now async
- What is the highest-risk area? Keychain access timeout and error handling
- How is that risk mitigated? Same timeout values, same error paths, just promisified

target.title: [Bug]: exec-approvals store lock leak wedges all exec into fail-closed deny (single gateway process)
target.body:
### Bug type

Gateway — tools / exec approvals (file locking)

### Beta release blocker

No (but arguably should be: it disables exec entirely for the standard Docker-on-macOS deployment within minutes of first use)

### Summary

Every acquisition of the exec-approvals store lock (`~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json.lock`) strands: the gateway acquires the
lock during exec evaluation, proceeds as if it released it, but the lock file remains on disk. Subsequent store access then fails — first
`file lock timeout`, then every exec in the process is denied fail-closed (`exec denied: host=gateway security=deny`), including trivially allowlisted commands (`ls`). Cron tooling fails too (`cron failed: file lock timeout` for plain `list`). Recovery requires externally deleting the lock file.

Measured strand rate: **7 out of 7 acquisitions** during one 2.5-minute agent run (see watchdog log below). The staleness detector correctly refuses to reclaim (owner PID alive, starttime matches), so the failure is permanent without intervention.

Likely interaction: the fail-closed persistence-error handling from #103515 ("prevent exec approval revocation races", 2026-07-10) + a lock release (unlink) that silently does not take effect on a Docker Desktop VirtioFS bind-mounted state dir.

### Steps to reproduce

 1. Fresh container start; verify no `exec-approvals.json.lock` exists and
   `openclaw approvals get --gateway` parses with `security=allowlist`.
2. Trigger an agent turn (chat or `/hooks/agent`) that issues several exec
   tool calls in sequence (a mix of allowlisted commands and one allowlist
   miss reproduces fastest).
3. Observe:
   - first exec evaluations return correct verdicts (`allowlist miss` —
     i.e. the store was readable),
   - within seconds one exec fails `file lock timeout for
     ~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json`,
   - all subsequent execs in the process fail
     `exec denied: host=gateway security=deny`, regardless of allowlist
     status,
   - concurrent readers starve permanently: an agent retrying
     `cron list` with escalating `timeoutMs` (10s → 20s → 30s → 60s → 90s)
     never succeeds over a 3-minute window.

### Expected behavior

- Lock released after each store access; failed release detected and   retried/logged.
- Allowlisted commands keep executing; a transient lock problem does not   permanently convert the effective policy to deny for the whole process.
- A process can reclaim a lock it provably owns (same pid + starttime +   nonce).

### Actual behavior

Timeline from a fresh container (single OpenClaw process, no CLI/TUI containers, `ask=off`):

```
21:10:40 gateway ready (no lock file; `approvals get` parses, security=allowlist)
21:11:16 exec denied: allowlist miss      <- store READ ok (correct verdict)
21:11:28 exec failed: file lock timeout   <- lock stranded by prior evaluation
21:11:30+ every exec: exec denied: host=gateway security=deny
          (including 8- and 10-char allowlisted commands)
```

Also reproduces with `security=full` at **every** layer (config `tools.exec`, per-agent `tools.exec`, approvals-file defaults + all agents): the effective-policy intersection still reads the approvals file, so policy content is irrelevant — first exec activity strands the lock and everything fails closed.

**Pristine-upstream reproduction (2026-07-15, timestamps local UTC+2):**
fresh container from unmodified upstream `main`, no lock sidecar at boot, watchdog workaround stopped. During a normal agent turn:

```
20:57:34Z lock sidecar created (see payload under Logs)
20:57:48+ exec denied: host=gateway security=deny  (5+ commands, 23–156 chars)
```

After externally deleting the lock, the **next** exec activity stranded a fresh sidecar (`createdAt 19:01:32Z`, same live owner), producing `file lock timeout` → `security=deny` again; deleting it a second time restored operation again. The leak is therefore per-acquisition: acquire → verdict returned → sidecar never removed → all later store access fails closed until external deletion.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.2, built from source. Reproduced on three builds:

- **unmodified upstream `main` tip of 2026-07-15** (`<PASTE SHA from
  ~/repos/openclaw: git rev-parse HEAD>`; image labeled `repro.sha`) — no
  fork commits
- fork = current `main` (aa04722 lineage, 2026-07-13) + one commit touching
  only OpenRouter request payloads (unrelated path)
- ~2026-07-10 main snapshot

### Operating system

macOS (Apple Silicon Mac mini) host; gateway runs in Docker (Debian bookworm-based image), Docker Desktop with **VirtioFS** file sharing. State dir `./config` bind-mounted to `/home/node/.openclaw`; gateway rootfs read-only; container user `node`; single gateway process (verified via /proc).

### Install method

Source build in a custom Docker image (`docker build` from the repo, run via docker compose). No npm-global/managed install.

## Model

`openrouter/minimax/minimax-m3` (default agent); other agents use `z-ai/glm-5.2`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`. Model choice has no effect on the bug (reproduced across all of them).

## Provider / routing chain

OpenRouter → openai-completions API. Not relevant to the bug (failure is in local exec-approvals store locking, before any provider involvement).

## Additional provider/model setup details

None relevant. `tools.exec.security=allowlist`, `ask=off`, `askFallback=deny`, `autoAllowSkills=on`; 7 configured agents with ~66
allowlist entries each. Approvals file validated (parses, unique ids). ### Additional provider/model setup details

**Lock owner forensics — owner is the live, healthy gateway process.**

From the pristine-upstream reproduction (2026-07-15):

```json
{ "pid": 22, "createdAt": "2026-07-15T18:57:34.477Z", "starttime": 8175917 }
```

```
$ docker exec openclaw-gateway sh -c 'tr "\0" " " < /proc/22/cmdline'
node dist/index.js gateway --bind lan --port 18789
$ docker exec openclaw-gateway sh -c "awk '{print \$22}' /proc/22/stat"
8175917      <- matches payload; owner alive while readers time out
```

Re-strand after external deletion (same run, next exec activity):

```json
{ "pid": 22, "createdAt": "2026-07-15T19:01:32.776Z", "starttime": 8175917 }
```

Original incident on the fork build (2026-07-13), identical signature:

```json
{ "pid": 22, "createdAt": "2026-07-13T05:49:47.879Z",
  "nonce": "93e2587a-0447-4f86-865e-1a19c7af6888", "starttime": 25098 }
```

```
$ docker exec openclaw-gateway sh -c 'tr "\0" " " < /proc/22/cmdline'
node dist/index.js gateway --bind lan --port 18789
$ docker exec openclaw-gateway sh -c "awk '{print \$22}' /proc/22/stat"
25098        <- matches lock payload; owner alive; lock hours old
```

**Reader starvation** (concurrent sessions; agent retrying `cron list` with
escalating timeouts, all failing across 3 minutes):

```
20:50:07 cron failed: file lock timeout ({"action":"list"})
20:50:14 ... timeoutMs:15000 -> timeout
20:50:26 ... timeoutMs:20000 -> timeout
20:50:35 ... timeoutMs:30000 -> timeout
20:51:06 ... timeoutMs:60000 -> timeout
20:52:07 ... timeoutMs:90000 -> timeout
```

**Watchdog proof + strand rate** — a sidecar deleting locks older than a few
seconds restores service mid-run and shows every acquisition strands:

```
Mon Jul 13 20:29:05 UTC 2026 reaped stranded exec-approvals lock (age 10s)
Mon Jul 13 20:29:47 UTC 2026 reaped stranded exec-approvals lock (age 10s)
Mon Jul 13 20:30:05 UTC 2026 reaped stranded exec-approvals lock (age 11s)
Mon Jul 13 20:30:38 UTC 2026 reaped stranded exec-approvals lock (age 10s)
Mon Jul 13 20:30:50 UTC 2026 reaped stranded exec-approvals lock (age  9s)
Mon Jul 13 20:31:02 UTC 2026 reaped stranded exec-approvals lock (age  9s)
Mon Jul 13 20:31:17 UTC 2026 reaped stranded exec-approvals lock (age 10s)
```

With the watchdog active, previously always-wedging agent runs complete
(`hook agent run completed`). Full `logging.level=debug` file logs and
stability bundles available on request.

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Covered by the log excerpts above (lock payload JSON, /proc owner
forensics, starvation sequence, watchdog reap log). Happy to attach the raw
debug log files to the issue thread.

## Impact and severity

High. On a standard Docker-on-macOS deployment, **all** exec is denied
within minutes of the first exec-tool use — allowlisted commands included —
until the lock file is deleted externally. Cron tool actions fail as
collateral. Severity is amplified by a security-relevant second-order
effect: because the failure surfaces as `security=deny`, agents interpret
it as policy and begin escalation attempts (retrying with
`host=sandbox/auto/node`, `elevated:true`, `pty:true`, `security:"approve"`,
and probing `.env`/`hosts.yml` for credentials).

## Additional information

Compounding behaviors worth fixing alongside:

1. Read path throws `file_lock_stale` on provably-stale locks instead of
   reclaiming, so a crash while holding the lock bricks exec across
   restarts.
2. Lock ownership (pid + starttime) assumes one PID namespace and stable
   boots — invalid across container restarts, SIGUSR1 in-process restarts,
   and sibling containers sharing the state dir.
3. With `ask=on-miss`, a pending approval (30-minute expiry) in one session
   starves all other sessions' exec and cron store access for the whole
   window — headless multi-agent setups fail closed everywhere.

Suggested directions: verify unlink success on release (retry + log);
allow same-pid+starttime+nonce re-acquisition to self-heal; or use
flock()/in-process locking for the single-process case instead of lock
files on a (possibly virtio/network) state dir.

Current user-side mitigation: a busybox sidecar deleting
`exec-approvals.json.lock` older than 3s — ugly, but restores full
operation with the allowlist enforced.

Happy to test instrumented builds or candidate fixes on this environment.

- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. target.title: refactor(gateway-client): expose request dispatch boundary
target.body:
Related: #96230

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-internal callers can observe a request result or a later `accepted` response, but cannot distinguish a failure before the request frame entered the local WebSocket transport from a failure after dispatch. That distinction is required before later restart-recovery work can make conservative retry or refund decisions without guessing from promise settlement.

This is the first independently reviewable dependency extracted from #96230. The original PR remains frozen while its behavior is split into ordered, narrower changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The protocol client is the only layer that owns the synchronous `socket.send(...)` boundary, so this adds an optional `onDispatched` observer immediately after `send` returns successfully and routes it through the existing callback-isolation helper. The package client and high-level `callGateway` wrapper forward the same observer without changing request frames, protocol versions, timeout/abort cleanup, reconnect behavior, or `onAccepted` response semantics.

The observer contract is intentionally narrow: it means the request frame was handed to the local WebSocket transport. It does not mean the Gateway/server accepted or processed the request. The request option type lives in a dedicated small module and is re-exported from the existing protocol-client module, preserving import and structural type compatibility. `GatewayClient` forwards that shared option shape as a unit, then overrides only its normalized `expectFinal` and `timeoutMs` values; this keeps the oversized implementation LOC-neutral without deleting unrelated comments.

This is a root-cause boundary fix: higher layers no longer need to infer whether transport dispatch happened. The gateway-client package is private and the new field is additive and optional. A consumer/test-double sweep covered the package export, OpenClaw facade, SDK transport, accepted-response caller, both affected request stubs, and the node-host bridge. The node-host bridge only forwards `timeoutMs` across its IPC boundary, so later recovery code must use `callGateway` or introduce a separate IPC dispatch acknowledgement rather than assuming this observer is available there.

Out of scope for this PR: Plugin SDK/session-state isolation, recovery persistence, `mainRestartRecovery` admission or ownership, bounded recovery, quarantine, and Doctor repair. In particular, this PR does not write any production recovery state.

## User Impact

There is no direct end-user behavior change. Existing callers behave exactly as before; later recovery PRs can use a precise local transport-dispatch fact instead of broad failure inference.

Risk is limited to an additive observer callback. It is not invoked when WebSocket send throws, observer exceptions are isolated from request settlement, and the callback must not be interpreted as server acceptance.

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
